newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says UK rate decision finely balanced.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK rate decision finely balanced.

text.p: The British economy is growing at a sustainable rate and the government is still aiming for 2.5 percent or lower inflation, British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday.
But the decision on interest rates remains "finely balanced," he said at a press conference.
Clarke said consumer demand was higher than last year but added that factory gate prices remained low and the pound "exceptionally strong."
"There are all sorts of factors which make this a finely balanaced judgement to where we are now within the monetary area," he said.
Clarke said he would meet with Bank of England Governor Eddie George next week when they would agree on how to sustain a lasting recovery with low inflation.
"The difference between myself and Eddie George is one quarter of one percent," he said. Clarke has refused several Bank of England requests for an increase in Britain's 6.0 percent interest rate.
Clarke said Britain was enjoying a prolonged economic recovery which would last as long as the government pursued its inflation target which he said it would continue to do.
"What we have is a growing economy, growing at a level which is sustainable," Clarke said.
The ruling Conservatives are more than 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party in the run-up to the May 1 election.
